clue.text: What happens is to get spotted about a certain age

indicators.note: the word for spotted goes round, or about, the other piece

parts.note: spotted means seen
something that happens is an event

explanation.surface: A teenager at a certain age breaks out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a teenager breaking out in spots; the definition is the age itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific number of years, the last of the teens, is one particular age.

clue.text: Direct and neat

definitions.meaning: to direct is to guide or ...
neat is an old word for cattle; a young bullock

explanation.definitionFit: To guide a course is to steer it, and a castrated bullock is one of the cattle once called neat.

clue.text: Girl vicars madly embrace — or the other way round

indicators.note: the scrambled clergymen wrap their arms around the girl
madly signals the letters going wild into a new order

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Clergymen hug a young woman wildly, or perhaps she hugs them.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled clergymen (VICRSA, from 'madly') hug the girl, so the definition neatly echoes the surface: one embracing the other, or the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is Latin for with the order reversed.

clue.text: Source of power from Blarney Stone?

definitions.text: Source of power from Blarney Stone?

parts.words: Source of power from Blarney Stone?
parts.note: blarney is smooth talk, so a born talker's gift of the gab is an inborn supply of hot air, read as a fuel

explanation.definitionFit: Methane piped from underground is a fuel, punned here as innate chatter from kissing the Irish Blarney Stone.

clue.text: Belts to send rig repair …

indicators.note: repair suggests the letters being fixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions about despatching a drilling rig for mending.
explanation.definitionFit: To engird is to encircle, as a belt goes round the waist.

clue.text: … necessary to end fuel spread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters scattered and laid out again

explanation.surface: Stopping fuel being scattered around is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is a slightly old-fashioned word for required or essential.

clue.text: Bell starts its sound to carry back

indicators.note: the start of the word Bell supplies its opening letter

parts.note: the sound a bell makes is a ring

explanation.surface: A bell begins chiming and carries its peal back to us.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to carry it here, back to where the speaker is.

clue.text: This and that …

parts.note: taken together, the one thing and the other thing, not just odds and ends

explanation.definitionFit: Both refers to two things together, one and the other.

clue.text: Rodent that's about to get ratty?

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes about, around, the rodent

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent about to turn bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for irritable or cross.

clue.text: One's not experienced corroded brass?

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument turned green with verdigris

explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a raw beginner, and a corroded brass instrument would literally be a green horn.

clue.text: Maintain the retailer's beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter is shifted from the beginning of the store's name to its end

parts.note: Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A shop must keep its opening spirit going right to the close.
explanation.walkthrough: TESCO is a UK supermarket chain; moving its T to the end gives ESCOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Escot is an archaic Shakespearean verb meaning to support or provide for someone.

clue.text: Angered at wild dog

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone furious lashes out at an untamed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a very large breed of domestic hound.

clue.text: Test possible artistic ability for "Showboat", say

parts.note: the Test is a Hampshire trout river, so Test is a possible example of a river
craft is skill in making things

explanation.surface: An audition tests whether a performer has the talent for the musical Showboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like a verb but is the River Test in Hampshire, England. A showboat is a Mississippi paddle steamer carrying a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A showboat is a paddle steamer with a theatre aboard, an example of a vessel used on inland waterways.

clue.text: Spare film director

definitions.meaning: spare in the sense of thin, with no fat

explanation.definitionFit: Spare and thin both describe a body without fat, and David Lean was a celebrated British director.

clue.text: Being erotic keeps animal endlessly on the hoof

indicators.note: the erotic word holds, keeps, the trimmed animal inside

parts.note: amatory means relating to sexual love

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the animal

parts.note: a bull is an animal

explanation.surface: Being amorous involves keeping a creature on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulatory means walking about, as cattle move while grazing.

clue.text: Youthful pastime lost by us oldies

definitions.meaning: a children's game played by rolling small glass balls
losing one's wits or mental faculties, in the idiom about going senile

explanation.definitionFit: Children play a game with little glass balls, and someone going senile is said to have lost them, an idiom for wits.

clue.text: Girl turns up to iron out place of relief for process that may include relief

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

indicators.note: out signals the metal's symbol being removed from the town

parts.note: Mafeking, a South African town, was famously relieved in the Boer War
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A woman arrives to smooth over a place of rest for a job involving relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' makes MAP from PAM; the relief of Mafeking (1900) was a famous Boer War event. Relief in the definition means relief maps showing height.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartography may show relief, the height of the land, on its maps.

clue.text: Chimney first built in the past brings back trouble

parts.note: lum is a Scots and northern English word for a chimney

indicators.note: only the first letter of built is wanted

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A chimney put up long ago causes trouble at the rear of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scottish word for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower part of the spine, a classic ailment of that region.

clue.text: With no charm an unlikely broadcaster to get this job

indicators.note: unlikely signals an improbable reworking of the letters

explanation.surface: A presenter with no charm is improbable for this job.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman presents and links a news broadcast.

clue.text: A time to put across and be conciliatory

indicators.note: the word for put lies across, around, the other letters

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a moment to reach out across a divide and make peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to soothe and appease, acting in a peacemaking way.

clue.text: Space for a couple to hug

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
a brace is a pair

explanation.surface: Room for two people to cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is to clasp someone in your arms.

clue.text: Cup soon ruined by a little drop

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A cup of tea is spoilt by just a tiny splash of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a very small amount, a trace or dash of something.

clue.text: Slut, English or Balkan

parts.note: a sloven is a slovenly person

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a slovenly person, whether English or from the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene comes from Slovenia, on the edge of the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: It may come in glasses for astigmatism

indicators.note: for introduces the word whose opening letters supply the wine, as if the answer were inside it

explanation.surface: Spectacles prescribed to correct a defect of vision.
explanation.walkthrough: The spectacle picture is the misdirection: the glasses are wine glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine, poured into a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Sense of state corruption

indicators.note: corruption degrades the word, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A feeling about corruption within the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses.

clue.text: "They abolish spats", said by a brother

indicators.note: said means the word for spats is spoken, giving something close in sound

parts.note: spats are short gaiters worn over shoes

explanation.surface: A monk declares that people who wear spats should be done away with.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate is to repeal or annul, so those who do it are abolishers.

clue.text: She finds much harassment upsetting

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the letters upside down
the woman finds herself inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman discovers that a great deal of harassment is distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' picks HARAS out of muCH HARASsment; 'upsetting' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a woman's name, so a female person.

clue.text: It's a very little matter, like half of our letters

definitions.meaning: read as A to M, the first half of the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny particle of matter, and split as A to M it spans thirteen of the twenty-six letters.

clue.text: Home at the weekend, one dined but was still hungry

parts.note: in means at home
Sat, short for Saturday, is part of the weekend
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Someone stays in at the weekend and eats, yet still wants more.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate is a poetic form of insatiable, describing an appetite never satisfied.

clue.text: In the old days insect left a shell

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the insect's letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: formerly means in the old days
a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: Long ago a creeping insect abandoned its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect's letters F, L, Y leave scattered from FORMERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible Channel Islands mollusc, an abalone prized for its ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Glow of genetic modification over pasture

indicators.note: the abbreviation spreads over, enclosing, the meadow word

parts.note: GM is the usual abbreviation for genetically modified
lea is a poetic word for meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: Genetically modified crops cast a glow over the grazing land.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a faint or brief shine of light.

clue.text: Very nice romp — and hard all the way

indicators.note: a romp is a boisterous frolic, so the letters tumble about

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A lovely frolic that was tough going from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch means completely, throughout, the whole distance.
